events.title: Arc browser launched
events.summary: The Browser Company released Arc in invite-only beta on April 19, 2022 — a Chromium-based browser rethinking tabs, spaces, and vertical sidebar navigation.
events.about: Arc treats the browser as a workspace: vertical tabs, split views, built-in note-taking, and per-space profiles. Built on Chromium by ex-Chrome engineers, it targeted designers and knowledge workers who wanted Safari-like polish with Chrome compatibility — influencing how startups think about browser UX.

narrative.whyChosen: Arc proved a startup could still reinvent browser chrome even on Chromium.
narrative.whyImportant: Its sidebar-and-spaces model inspired copycats and renewed interest in browser innovation.
narrative.problemSolved: Tab overload and cluttered browser UI had not changed meaningfully since Chrome's minimal bar.

events.title: Node.js 18 released
events.summary: Node.js 18.0.0 shipped on April 19, 2022 with a fetch API, test runner module, and V8 10.1.
events.about: Node 18 became LTS in October 2022 — bringing browser-standard `fetch` to server code without `node-fetch`, and previewing a built-in test runner. It powered Next.js 13+, Vercel edge functions, and AWS Lambda runtimes through 2024.

narrative.whyChosen: Node 18's native fetch removed a ubiquitous npm dependency from server JavaScript.
narrative.whyImportant: LTS 18 aligned Node with web platform APIs developers already knew.
narrative.problemSolved: Server code needed polyfills for fetch and struggled with ESM migration friction.
